title: SLES 12 SP3: isolating an NRPE TLS handshake failure
text: This procedure documents a user-performed diagnostic on SLES 12 SP3 with NRPE 2.15-4.24 , OpenSSL 1.0.2j-fips and a monitoring host running check_nrpe 4.1.0 . The original daemon reported Error: Could not complete SSL handshake. 1 . A separate plaintext test returned NRPE_PLAIN_OK . Hostnames and addresses below are anonymized examples. The test runs a second NRPE instance on TCP 15666 , with its own configuration and PID file. The existing service on TCP 5666 , its configuration and Nagios check definitions remain unchanged. No package installation, systemd override, daemon-reload or production service restart is needed. Plaintext is a temporary diagnostic, not a deployment recommendation: the test has no TLS encryption or certificate authentication. Use a trusted network and restrict access to the monitoring host. Stop the test instance afterwards. Example hosts and prerequisites Role Example hostname Example address Monitoring host with check_nrpe monitor01 192.0.2.10 SLES 12 SP3 host with NRPE 2.15 sles-agent01 192.0.2.20 The addresses belong to a documentation range. Replace them with your actual addresses before running the commands. server_address must be assigned to the SLES host; allowed_hosts must contain the source address the monitoring host actually uses. Check the hostname before working on either machine. On the SLES host, inspect the platform and local addresses: hostname cat /etc/os-release /usr/sbin/nrpe -V ip -4 addr show sudo ss -ltnp | grep ':15666' Expect SLES VERSION_ID="12.3" and NRPE 2.15. An NRPE version/usage command may exit nonzero after printing its output. Port 15666 must be unused; no output from the final command is expected before starting the test. If a previous test directory or instance exists, inspect and clean it up before reusing these paths. Allow TCP 15666 only from the monitoring host if a firewall change is necessary; record and later remove only that temporary rule. 1. Create the isolated configuration on the SLES host NRPE 2.15 does not support the foreground option -f . Use its daemon option -d with -n to disable TLS for this instance only. A modern ssl_... setting in the configuration is not a substitute for that startup option. sudo install -d -o root -g nagios -m 0750 /run/nrpe-plain-test sudo install -d -o nagios -g nagios -m 0750 /run/nrpe-plain-test/runtime sudo tee /run/nrpe-plain-test/nrpe.cfg > /dev/null << 'EOF' server_address=192.0.2.20 server_port=15666 pid_file=/run/nrpe-plain-test/runtime/nrpe.pid nrpe_user=nagios nrpe_group=nagios allowed_hosts=192.0.2.10 dont_blame_nrpe=0 command_timeout=10 connection_timeout=10 command[check_plain_test]=/usr/bin/printf 'NRPE_PLAIN_OK\n' EOF sudo chown root:nagios /run/nrpe-plain-test/nrpe.cfg sudo chmod 0640 /run/nrpe-plain-test/nrpe.cfg sudo -u nagios test -r /run/nrpe-plain-test/nrpe.cfg \ && echo 'Test configuration is readable' The root-owned configuration is readable by nagios ; its runtime subdirectory allows that account to write the separate PID file. Command arguments remain disabled. The test defines only a fixed printf command, not production checks. 2. Start and inspect the test instance on the SLES host sudo -u nagios /usr/sbin/nrpe \ -c /run/nrpe-plain-test/nrpe.cfg -d -n sudo ss -ltnp | grep ':15666' With -d , the prompt returns because the daemon runs in the background. Confirm that ss shows NRPE listening on the chosen local address and port 15666 before testing remotely. A returned prompt alone does not establish successful startup. For startup errors: sudo journalctl -t nrpe --since '5 minutes ago' --no-pager If you change this configuration later, stop only the test instance using the PID procedure below, then repeat this start command. No systemd reload is required for the separate daemon. 3. Run the check from the monitoring host /usr/lib/nagios/plugins/check_nrpe \ -H 192.0.2.20 -p 15666 -2 -n -c check_plain_test Adjust the plugin path if needed. -2 selects the packet format understood by NRPE 2.15; -n selects plaintext, matching the test daemon. Do not modify global Nagios command definitions or remove TLS from other hosts' checks. Expected output: NRPE_PLAIN_OK This is the result reported by the user for the original SLES 12 SP3 host. It confirms reachability on the test port, access acceptance and execution of this fixed command without TLS. It narrows the original problem toward TLS negotiation, but does not identify a specific cipher/certificate cause, test the production port or commands, or prove an upgrade has fixed the real deployment. Troubleshooting encountered during this procedure Symptom Meaning and next step invalid option -- 'f' NRPE 2.15 lacks -f ; start this test with -d -n . Unable to open config file ... for reading Check the file's root:nagios ownership, 0640 mode and directory traversal permissions. chmod 0640 alone leaves a root-group file unreadable to nagios . Cannot assign requested address The configured address is not local to this host. Check hostname and ip -4 addr show ; make sure you are on the intended SLES server. Connection refused Check for a listener with ss and inspect startup logs; also consider an actively rejecting firewall. This happens before NRPE/TLS negotiation. Receive header underflow Not a specific TLS diagnosis. Confirm both ends use -n , the client uses -2 , and the address/port are correct; inspect server logs, allowed_hosts and any TCP-wrapper rules. Timeout Check routing, firewall policy and the actual listening address. Do not disable the firewall globally. rmdir: Directory not empty The runtime subdirectory or PID file remains. Stop the test and remove those specific paths in the order below. The old daemon also reported disable_syslog=0 as an unknown configuration option in the original production configuration. That is separate from the TLS failure; this minimal test configuration intentionally omits that directive. 4. Stop the test and remove its files on the SLES host Inspect the PID and command first. It must refer to the separate instance using /run/nrpe-plain-test/nrpe.cfg , not the production NRPE daemon: sudo ps -p "$( sudo cat /run/nrpe-plain-test/runtime/nrpe.pid)" \ -o pid,user,args After confirming that identity, stop that process: sudo kill "$( sudo cat /run/nrpe-plain-test/runtime/nrpe.pid)" sudo ss -ltnp | grep ':15666' Wait until port 15666 has no listener. If the PID file is missing or stale, use ss and process inspection to identify the test process; do not use killall nrpe , stop the production service, or send a signal to an unverified PID. Then remove the specific test files and directories: sudo rm -f /run/nrpe-plain-test/runtime/nrpe.pid sudo rm /run/nrpe-plain-test/nrpe.cfg sudo rmdir /run/nrpe-plain-test/runtime sudo rmdir /run/nrpe-plain-test Remove any firewall exception added specifically for this diagnostic. Existing production files and the listener on port 5666 are unaffected. The test paths under /run are temporary and do not survive reboot. For the certificate-authenticated upgrade path, see the SLES 12 SP3 build guide and SLES TLS configuration example . The project's NRPE 4.1.1 container tests are separate evidence from this user-performed plaintext diagnostic.

title: SLES 12 SP3 RPM target
text: The affected deployment is SLES 12 SP3 , confirmed by /etc/os-release on 2026-10-28. Its original package is NRPE 2.15-4.24 , linked to libssl.so.1.0.0 and libcrypto.so.1.0.0 . Previous SLES 15 SP3/SP4 test results do not validate this platform. The active target is now sles12sp3 ; old releases are not overwritten or relabeled. python3 nrpe.py verify sles12sp3 python3 nrpe.py test sles12sp3 Use --rebuild to deliberately replace existing local outputs. Old SLE-15 RPMs must not be installed or copied into this target's output directory. Build architecture and matching inputs The native build and runtime stages use SUSE's genuine image, pinned to: registry.suse.com/suse/sles12sp3@sha256:0995dbf051274a3a5baf19c7f94ce7ebe69d7aa91f7b3b22248bd06d7122e53a Its identity is ID=sles , VERSION_ID=12.3 , x86_64, with RPM 4.11.2 and OpenSSL 1.0.2j. SLES_BASE_IMAGE can select an approved equivalent, but the native guard rejects other distributions/releases and requires the OpenSSL 1.0 ABI. The runtime image contains no compiler or preinstalled NRPE server. The historical image has no configured repositories and the old SP3 backports index is empty. Instead, the bootstrap manifest pins original SLE-12 GA/SP3 Server and SDK RPMs available through SUSE's public OBS API. Each entry records its original URL, size, SHA-256, name, version, architecture, vendor and SUSE signing key. No SLE-15 or Leap package is used. A separate Python download stage fetches and hash-checks those RPMs and the pinned OBS sources. A company CA is added only to that process's TLS context; it is not copied into target packages. The actual SLES stage independently checks the pinned RPM hashes, required SUSE signatures and package identities before installing anything. Downloads are not treated as signature verification. Native installation uses the complete local dependency set, retaining normal RPM dependency checks; no registration credentials or license terms are supplied or accepted by this workflow. No system OpenSSL replacement is required. Python is not needed in the old target image. NRPE and its support packages are compiled/packaged by SLES 12's own tools. The former --sles-media option and SLE-15 module/ISO layout were removed; an ISO is not required by this workflow. Sources and package identities NRPE : reviewed immutable OBS revision 835292739a5736a9d8f0460f670b6f15 , version 4.1.1 , local Release 0.withargs1 . Command arguments remain compiled in, runtime-disabled by default; Bash command substitution stays disabled. This is a native rebuild, not a reproduction of the old installed NRPE 2.15 package. Nagios build macros : immutable OBS revision a911087cc73b87e04465861110d43754 , version 0.14-0 , built natively. The upstream spec explicitly supports SLES 12. This build dependency is not faked or supplied by a SLE-15 binary. Nagios user package : pinned original system-user-nagios 1.0.0-0 , built natively after the macros. Existing users and groups are handled by the original package scripts. output/sles12sp3/ contains the server, matching monitoring-plugins-nrpe client, real user-package RPM, all three source RPMs, four input manifests, original OBS files including history, and SHA256SUMS for all three binary RPMs. The macros' build-only binary is not a runtime dependency or release asset. Its corresponding source and BSD notice are included for rebuilding the workflow. The source/license gate checks every original input and SRPM member, the client/server source/version relationship, the bootstrap manifest and component notices. See license evidence and the notice directory . TLS and the original handshake failure The operator later clarified that starting the missing nrpe.service restored the checks in their combined Nagios/NRPE setup. Check the services-first FAQ before replacing packages. That service-state fix did not require a custom build and is separate from the old binary's certificate-authentication limitations. For the user-performed pre-upgrade diagnostic with NRPE 2.15 and check_nrpe 4.1.0, see isolating an NRPE TLS handshake failure . It documents a separate temporary plaintext instance, the successful result and cleanup using anonymized hosts and documentation addresses, without modifying the production service or reloading systemd. NRPE 2.15 uses legacy anonymous DH. Merely enabling services or adding modern configuration directives does not add certificate support to that old binary. This build supplies NRPE 4.1.1 and a matching client against the existing OpenSSL 1.0 ABI. The integration test explicitly requires TLS 1.2 , excludes anonymous authentication, requires a client certificate and checks rejected/enabled command arguments. It does not weaken cipher settings or disable certificate verification to make the test pass. TLS 1.3 is not supported by OpenSSL 1.0.2 and is not claimed. For the deployed server, back up the old package/configuration, review included files and configure compatible CA/server/client certificates on both ends. Build-time --ca-cert does not provision production NRPE TLS. The FAQ distinguishes service startup from TLS compatibility. Use the SLES-specific DHE-RSA configuration : NRPE 4.1.1 needs DH initialization enabled together with an explicit cipher list that excludes anonymous authentication. The modern-client test passed with OpenSSL 3.5.7, verified server hostname/chain and a separate required client certificate; a connection without that client certificate was rejected. Recorded validation and limits The target is published; see the release history for exact master-commit, CI and independently checked release-asset evidence. Earlier local migration runs are retained in that history. A fresh clean-checkout run is required for every release candidate; historical results do not replace it. Container tests run NRPE directly. They do not validate real-server systemd, reboot, site-specific commands, production certificates, update or rollback. Use installation , rollback and practical validation before deployment. The SUSE lifecycle lists SLES 12 SP3 general support end as 2019-06-30 and LTSS end as 2022-06-30. This is a requested legacy compatibility build, not extended vendor maintenance or certification. Historical package/image availability can change and does not guarantee security support.

title: Build and NRPE diagnostics
text: Failed workflow commands retain their original exit status and raw output in the local run log. Recognized failures add contextual hints. Successful commands do not emit failure hints, including when a retry recovered from an earlier error. Hints classify observed messages; they do not establish a root cause. Inspect an existing log python3 nrpe.py diagnose ./build.log python3 nrpe.py diagnose ./build.log --ca-configured python3 nrpe.py diagnose ./redacted-nrpe.log --context nrpe diagnose reads a local text file without Docker or a connection to the server. It executes no log content, prints category hints rather than raw lines, and does not mark any workflow as passed. Exit 0 means the file was read successfully, not that the recorded build/check succeeded. No recognized failure is not a pass. Use --ca-configured only when the recorded build was actually given a CA. The default context is build/download failures. Use --context nrpe for daemon or check_nrpe logs: build-time CA configuration and deployed client/server TLS are separate. On servers without Python, review/redact the log and copy it to the workstation running this tool. Never share credentials, private keys or full environment dumps. Keep raw local logs outside Git. Interpret the categories Observed error What to check Issuer unknown / certificate verification failed Build: issuing CA and chain, certificate dates/name and clock. If company HTTPS inspection is used, pass its reviewed CA with --ca-cert or NRPE_CA_CERT . A supplied CA does not guarantee it is the right issuer. Expired certificate / hostname mismatch Correct the certificate, endpoint or clock; adding an unrelated CA cannot fix these. Image/frontend pull trust failure Configure trust in Docker Desktop/Engine and BuildKit. The build's --ca-cert does not configure engine trust. Proxy authentication / HTTP 407 Proxy reachability and credentials for the affected component. A CA cannot fix proxy authentication. DNS resolution failure Name resolution on the host and inside the affected Docker component, including VPN/proxy configuration. Missing or expired repository metadata Actual suite/service pack, repository URL, access rights and clock. Do not disable signatures/validity or substitute another distribution. Checksum, signature or pinned-input mismatch Stop and investigate the reviewed source/key/hash. Do not replace hashes or bypass signatures to obtain a pass. No space left Host and Docker storage separately. Preview local cleanup ; it does not prune BuildKit caches or delete current packages. Connection refused Intended address/port, listener, daemon startup logs and any firewall REJECT. The connection failed before TLS negotiation. NRPE on a deployed SLES 12 SP3 host For Could not complete SSL handshake. 1 , compare both NRPE and OpenSSL versions, TLS versions, shared authenticated ciphers and CA/server/client certificate settings. The message alone does not prove that a CA is missing. NRPE 2.15's legacy anonymous DH and NRPE 4.x certificate authentication are different modes. Receive header underflow can also result from mismatched TLS modes/packet versions or access rejection. Check -2 for NRPE 2.x, allowed_hosts , TCP wrappers and simultaneous server logs before attributing it to certificates. The anonymized SLES 12 SP3 diagnostic records the separate plaintext test, unsupported -f option, configuration permissions, wrong-host bind error and cleanup. Plaintext is temporary test evidence, not a production fix. Use the authenticated TLS configuration for the custom NRPE 4.1.1 build. Do not apply modern ssl_* directives or disable_syslog=0 to an NRPE 2.15 configuration. Inspect the real service definition and process command before changing startup options. A manually started daemon is not managed by systemd; a failed second service start can simply mean its port/PID is already occupied. Do not launch another instance or remove live locks to hide that condition.

title: Updating and rolling back a deployed package
text:
These are target-server procedures, not nrpe.py commands. Start with the installation guide and the upstream manuals . Use a maintenance window and test the process on an equivalent disposable server before a production rollout. Container package/protocol tests do not exercise your server's service manager, firewall, local checks, or configuration migration. Before an update Record the installed package version, distribution, service state, configuration locations and a known successful check from the actual monitoring server. Keep the exact previously installed server package and its original checksum manifest in a local previous/ directory. Keep exactly one server version there. An installed custom package may not be downloadable from a repository; a filesystem/configuration backup alone cannot recreate its original binary. Preserve root-only backups of configuration, included snippets, custom scripts, ownership/permissions, service overrides, TLS certificates and private keys. Keys may live outside the main configuration directory. Do not commit or upload these backups, and do not assume this project's build CA backs them up. Build and verify the replacement for the exact destination release. Transfer it into a separate replacement/ directory and check SHA256SUMS there. Preserve the previous build outputs before using --rebuild on a workstation. Review version/configuration differences and dependency changes. If a package transaction would remove unrelated monitoring components or replace a shared user package, stop and resolve that change first. Example root-only configuration backups, run on the destination. Save the printed backup path; use that same path when restoring, rather than creating a new one. For Debian: nrpe_backup_dir = "/var/backups/nrpe-custom/$( date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)" sudo install -d -m 0700 " $nrpe_backup_dir " sudo cp -a /etc/nagios " $nrpe_backup_dir /nagios" dpkg-query -W -f= '${Package} ${Version} ${Architecture}
' nagios-nrpe-server | sudo tee " $nrpe_backup_dir /installed-package.txt" > /dev/null printf 'Backup directory: %s
' " $nrpe_backup_dir " For SLES 12 SP3: nrpe_backup_dir = "/var/backups/nrpe-custom/$( date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)" sudo install -d -m 0700 " $nrpe_backup_dir " sudo cp -a /etc/nrpe.cfg " $nrpe_backup_dir /nrpe.cfg" rpm -q nrpe system-user-nagios | sudo tee " $nrpe_backup_dir /installed-package.txt" > /dev/null printf 'Backup directory: %s
' " $nrpe_backup_dir " These examples back up the standard main configuration only. Add every configured include directory, local plugin/wrapper, service override and external TLS file to the backup before changing the installation. On SLES, inspect the configuration for the actual include paths; do not assume Debian's layout. Install and check the replacement Install the explicit local file from replacement/ using APT or zypper as in the installation guide . Package scripts can start or restart NRPE; use your site's maintenance/access controls during the transaction. Review configuration prompts rather than automatically forcing new or old files. After installation: Confirm the intended custom version with dpkg-query -W nagios-nrpe-server or rpm -q nrpe ; inspect package-created .dpkg-dist , .dpkg-old , .rpmnew and .rpmsave files where present. Merge configuration deliberately, keeping allowed hosts, reviewed command definitions, TLS settings and disabled Bash substitution. Do not automatically enable dont_blame_nrpe simply because the new binary supports arguments. Restart the appropriate service and inspect systemctl status and journalctl using the commands in the installation guide. Repeat the known check from the real monitoring server with its production TLS settings. Check both a normal result and the argument policy you actually use. If the package installs but checks fail, retain the transaction/service logs and identify whether the cause is configuration, missing plugins, TLS, access rules, or the binary. Reinstalling a package alone does not restore configuration. Debian rollback Change into the saved previous/ directory and verify its original checksum file. The following intentionally permits a version downgrade to the local file: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS sudo systemctl stop nagios-nrpe-server sudo apt install --allow-downgrades ./nagios-nrpe-server_ * _amd64.deb Set nrpe_backup_dir to the saved path from before the update, then restore the reviewed configuration and original ownership/permissions: sudo cp -a " $nrpe_backup_dir /nagios/." /etc/nagios/ sudo systemctl restart nagios-nrpe-server sudo systemctl status nagios-nrpe-server --no-pager dpkg-query -W nagios-nrpe-server Compare the active include tree with the backup. Copying files back does not remove snippets introduced by the failed update; inspect and reconcile those before restarting. Restore separately backed-up TLS files, wrappers and service overrides as needed. Package scripts may restart the service during rollback too. SLES 12 SP3 rollback From the saved previous/ directory: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS sudo systemctl stop nrpe sudo rpm --upgrade --oldpackage --verbose --hash ./nrpe-[0-9] * .x86_64.rpm --oldpackage deliberately allows the older saved binary after its original checksum is verified. Normal RPM dependency/payload checks stay enabled; resolve prerequisites using matching SLES-12 repositories. Keep the real Nagios user; restoring an older server does not require removing a shared user package. With nrpe_backup_dir set to the saved pre-update backup path: sudo cp -a " $nrpe_backup_dir /nrpe.cfg" /etc/nrpe.cfg sudo systemctl restart nrpe sudo systemctl status nrpe --no-pager rpm -q nrpe Also restore/reconcile included snippets, TLS files, scripts and overrides from their backups. Compare .rpmnew / .rpmsave files rather than treating either as the authoritative configuration automatically. Repeat the original remote check. After recovery Confirm the old package version and production checks actually work again. If a dependency transaction changed other packages, assess those separately; restoring NRPE alone is not a whole-system rollback. Use your system backup/recovery process if the host is unresponsive or package operations are no longer possible. A version hold/lock can be a temporary operational choice, but it can also block security updates. Record the reason, owner and review date rather than silently pinning an old custom package forever. See the maintenance policy .

title: Documentation website and GitHub Pages
text: The website is static HTML/CSS/JavaScript with no analytics, remote fonts, submission database or hosted backend. Existing Markdown remains the source of documentation. The builder rewrites internal links, creates a local search index and checks every generated internal link/anchor. Original third-party notices are copied without changing their text. Presentation and field notes live under website/ . English matches the project documentation. The initial SLES note uses only reported observations, not an invented testimonial or production TLS claim. New reports follow the field-note guide . Homepage content and CLI capture The hero's "Built from real problems." line gently fades out, then reveals letters 70 ms apart with a 180 ms fade and small vertical transition per letter. Cycles start 60 seconds apart, leaving the complete sentence visible between cycles. Letter spacing stays reserved so the heading does not move while typing. Reduced-motion preferences and missing JavaScript keep the full heading static. Animation stops while the tab or heading is hidden. Returning to the heading preserves the scheduled interval; an elapsed interval starts a fresh 60-second wait instead of immediately replaying. There is no visible animation control. Screen readers receive the complete sentence once, without repeated announcements. The homepage links to GitHub's latest release rather than hardcoding a release version. Its supported-target table is derived from the README table, keeping target names and package formats in one source. The project story summarizes the reported troubleshooting; it does not claim a successful production upgrade. website/assets/cli-help.png shows actual python3 nrpe.py --help output captured from application revision 8a2b3d33c0fa . It is a static terminal view, not a live session or a successful build result. Refresh it when the command list changes: capture that command's output, render it as plain escaped text in a local terminal-style browser view, and take a screenshot. Keep machine names, paths and private infrastructure out of the capture. No screenshot tooling is required to build or use the website. website/assets/terminal-menu.png shows the current menu rendered by prompt_toolkit in an empty temporary workspace. Its actual terminal screen cells were captured at 100 columns by 24 rows and rendered as escaped text for the screenshot. It shows no successful build or real infrastructure; the homepage and menu guide share this image. Refresh it when navigation or presentation changes, preserving the same empty-workspace provenance. FAQ structure The FAQ remains canonical Markdown: level-two headings define topics, level-three headings define questions, and level-four headings divide longer answers. Keep existing heading IDs stable so shared troubleshooting links work. The website derives a compact question index, per-question links and its page outline from these headings; answers stay visible without JavaScript. Local search filters questions and their index entries, highlights matching prose, and provides a clear empty/reset state. It leaves command text intact. Opening a link to a filtered answer restores its context. The existing page outline tracks the current section; mobile uses one content column. Diagrams and wide tables Mermaid flowcharts and sequence diagrams are rendered into static SVG images at build time with Mermaid 12.2.0 and Puppeteer 25.16.0. Install local Chrome or Chromium on the website build workstation; set NRPE_WEBSITE_BROWSER to its executable if automatic discovery does not find it. CI uses its runner's Chrome. The browser loads Mermaid only through a temporary loopback HTTP server and blocks other requests. Package lifecycle scripts and automatic browser downloads remain disabled. The NRPE CLI and destination servers need none of these tools. Diagrams use strict mode and plain SVG text; external resources, active SVG content and per-diagram configuration overrides are rejected. Each figure has an accessible label, a full-size link and collapsed source. Visitors need no Mermaid runtime or JavaScript to see diagrams. Tables expose keyboard-focusable horizontal scrolling when needed; code and URL tokens stay intact rather than wrapping their final characters onto separate lines. Local preview Fenced code blocks use Shiki 4.5.0 with the bundled GitHub Dark Default theme. Shell/Bash, PowerShell, INI, Python, YAML, JSON, Dockerfile and diff use Shiki's existing TextMate grammars. NRPE snippets use a small project-owned TextMate grammar for flat directives, full-line comments, command[name] , $ARGn$ and upstream build-template placeholders. General INI and NRPE files are distinct languages; see the configuration reference . Colors and font styles come from the theme, including token background colors. The Python builder turns tokens into scoped CSS classes so no inline style or browser highlighter is needed. No Shiki runtime, grammar, WASM, CDN or remote font is loaded by visitors. Code text, indentation, entities and Unicode are checked for exact preservation before publication. Plain/unknown languages remain unchanged; Mermaid renders as static diagrams; there is no speculative language detection. Use Node.js 24 LTS and Python 3.9+ on the website build workstation. Neither Node nor website dependencies are needed for the NRPE CLI or destination servers. Install locked npm dependencies without package lifecycle scripts: npm ci --prefix website --ignore-scripts --no-fund python3 -m venv .nrpe/site-venv .nrpe/site-venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-website.txt .nrpe/site-venv/bin/python website/build.py python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory .nrpe/site The renderer runs local Node processes with bounded timeouts and caches repeated code batches during a build. It never downloads grammars while rendering. Missing Node/dependencies are build errors with installation guidance, not silent plain- text publication. CI audits both the npm lockfile and Python renderer requirements. Open http://localhost:8000/nrpe-custom/ . On Windows use .nrpe\site-venv\Scripts\python.exe for environment-local Python commands. The production base path is /nrpe-custom ; builds for another path cannot be published by the guarded publisher. Rebuilds replace only a directory carrying this builder's manifest; arbitrary directories, unknown added files and the workflow-state root are refused. In-checkout output belongs under .nrpe/site/<name> , not .nrpe itself. The website workflow tests rendering, links and publication guards and uploads a preview artifact. It never commits or publishes automatically, preserving human-only Git authorship. Reviewed publication to gh-pages Work on a topic branch, review and integrate into develop. Publication requires a separate explicit maintainer request. From the exact clean develop or master commit that should be shown on the website: .nrpe/site-venv/bin/python website/build.py .nrpe/site-venv/bin/python website/publish.py .nrpe/site-venv/bin/python website/publish.py --push The default is a read-only preview. --push checks source identity, base path, all asset hashes and the human author/committer. A separate temporary Git index creates a commit containing only the generated website, without replacing the source checkout/index. Deployment history is appended on gh-pages with an ordinary fast-forward push, never force-pushed. Concurrent changes are rejected. Master/develop are not deployment targets and must never be deleted. Do not develop features directly on gh-pages or edit generated HTML by hand. The site does not update itself after a master push. Rebuild and explicitly publish a reviewed commit when docs change; automatic package releases remain a separate workflow. GitHub Pages setup by the repository owner The requested hosting source is gh-pages , repository root. In GitHub: Open Settings → Pages . Select Deploy from a branch . Select gh-pages , / (root) , then save. Wait for deployment and verify the homepage, FAQ and a deep link. The expected URL is https://nojokefna.github.io/nrpe-custom/ . The repository visibility is managed by the owner and is not changed by the publisher. Pages availability and site visibility depend on GitHub's plan and settings. Review content for public disclosure; never include private logs, actual infrastructure addresses or keys. If the connected integration cannot access the Pages settings API, the owner must complete setup in Settings. A pushed branch alone does not prove the website is live. Deployment and HTTP/browser checks must complete before claiming successful hosting. See GitHub Pages setup .

title: Workflow reference
text: Build Debian nagios-nrpe-server packages and a SLES 12 SP3 nrpe RPM using the distribution packaging recipes, with command arguments compiled in and runtime argument handling disabled by default. Requirements Python 3.9 or newer; direct commands have no third-party Python dependencies. Optional arrow-key menu: from the repository root, use python3 -m pip install -r requirements-menu.txt . Docker Engine with BuildKit, Linux containers, and Docker Compose 2.17 or newer. Access from containers to the matching Debian or SLES/OBS repositories. Disk space for builder images, source trees, test images, and packages. Any editor can be used. On Windows, Docker Desktop with Linux containers is a suitable Docker runtime. ARM hosts need support for linux/amd64 emulation. Bash is needed inside containers and for optional local shell syntax checks. Quick start Use nrpe.py as the main entry point. It coordinates this project's Compose files, checks Docker readiness, and records results. Direct Compose commands bypass the controller's checks, logs, and target locks. From the repository root on Windows, Linux, or macOS: python3 nrpe.py doctor python3 nrpe.py verify debian12 Ensure that python3 --version reports Python 3.9 or newer. On Windows, make sure your Python installation provides python3 in PATH. Run without arguments for an interactive action and target menu: python3 nrpe.py The arrow-key menu returns after each command. Use arrows and Enter to navigate, Space to toggle targets, and A to select all targets. Escape returns to the previous screen; Ctrl+C exits the menu or interrupts a running command. Install the optional dependencies first; see the menu guide . Without an interactive terminal, no arguments prints help and does not prompt. All CLI messages are in English. Use --help or <command> --help for command-specific usage. Commands Command Purpose doctor Check required project files, Docker connectivity, Linux container mode, Compose v2, and both Compose configurations build <targets> Build packages, run in-container package checks, and verify exported checksums test <targets> Install and test existing packages without rebuilding them verify <targets> Build and integration-test each target before proceeding to the next status Show current packages, SHA-256 hashes, matching test results, and target locks without needing Docker logs --last Display output from the latest recorded workflow run logs --run <id> Display output from a particular recorded workflow run Select one target, multiple targets, or all by itself: python3 nrpe.py verify debian12 debian13 python3 nrpe.py verify all python3 nrpe.py test debian14 python3 nrpe.py status python3 nrpe.py logs -- last SLES 12 SP3 uses a genuine digest-pinned 12.3 image and a hash-pinned set of original SLE-12 Server/SDK RPMs. A modern input stage downloads sources; native SLES tools verify package signatures and compile/install the result. No SLE-15 binary or ISO layout is used, and the obsolete --sles-media option is removed. See the SLES guide . Targets and package builds Target Distribution Architecture Output directory debian11 Debian 11 Bullseye amd64 output/debian11/ debian12 Debian 12 Bookworm amd64 output/debian12/ debian13 Debian 13 Trixie amd64 output/debian13/ debian14 Debian 14 Forky amd64 output/debian14/ sles12sp3 SLES 12 SP3 x86_64 output/sles12sp3/ all includes every target, including the SLES target. To validate only Debian, list debian11 debian12 debian13 debian14 explicitly. Debian 11's security package files have moved to archive.debian.org ; the setup helper updates that security repository URL in both builder and test images. Suite names, signing keys, signature checks, and validity checks remain enabled. Debian 11 has been built and installation/TLS argument tests have passed here with 4.0.3-1+withargs1 . This is historical archive availability, not a promise of ongoing security updates for this old release. SLES uses an actual SLES 12 SP3 base, not a Debian or Leap replacement. Its RPM recipe, pinned sources, prerequisites, and validation limits are documented in SLES 12 SP3 . Each Debian target uses a corresponding Debian container with a shared Dockerfile. The build enables source repositories, installs build dependencies, and fetches verified official nagios-nrpe sources from the selected suite. Source versions are discovered dynamically; Forky is a moving testing suite. The Debian build changes only the intended configure option in debian/rules and the custom version entry in debian/changelog . It rejects unsupported packaging layouts. dpkg-buildpackage produces binary packages; the exported server keeps the name nagios-nrpe-server and uses ${original_version}+withargs1 . Do not implement versioning by renaming finished packages. Increment the custom revision when changing the recipe for the same official source version. The build verifies package identity, version, architecture, executable contents, and configure macros before exporting the server .deb , SHA256SUMS , and available .buildinfo . It also builds the corresponding source package before the binary build. output/debianXX/sources/ contains the custom .dsc , every upstream/packaging archive referenced by its SHA-256 fields, and a separate SHA256SUMS . Export rejects missing files, mismatched versions and hashes, and unsafe filenames. Preserve this directory alongside binaries for release preparation; the binary-only checksum file used for installation is unchanged. The client plugin is not exported. Existing valid output is retained until a replacement build passes its package and source checks. Installation and argument integration tests verify builds and tests a package; test exercises an existing artifact. Separate opt-in services in compose.test.yaml use docker/debian/test.Dockerfile to: Require exactly one server package and verify its checksum, identity, architecture, and custom version suffix. Install that local .deb and its dependencies in a fresh matching distribution container, then check the installed version. Confirm that the installed package keeps dont_blame_nrpe=0 by default. Start NRPE with a disposable configuration and confirm that ordinary requests succeed while argument requests are rejected. Set dont_blame_nrpe=1 only in the temporary configuration, restart NRPE, and verify exact responses for the argument pairs alpha beta and gamma delta . Debian's nagios-nrpe-plugin and the natively built SLES monitoring-plugins-nrpe supply check_nrpe , the client used by Nagios. A full Nagios scheduler or web interface is unnecessary for this protocol test. Client and server run inside the same container over loopback using TLS and a short-lived test certificate. No NRPE port is published. Package outputs are mounted read-only, and the installed default configuration is unchanged. Each target has a builder image and a separate minimal test image. Keeping tests separate ensures that compiler and build dependencies cannot hide missing runtime dependencies during package installation. Common Debian layers are shared by Docker, and cached images are reused. Tests do not need a full Nagios server image. An installation success alone does not mean the argument tests passed. The log explicitly reports argument rejection with dont_blame_nrpe=0 and exact argument responses with dont_blame_nrpe=1 . These tests need the target distribution's repository access and run NRPE directly. They do not validate systemd startup, external network access, production certificates, or a complete Nagios deployment. Exact all-five-target release results are recorded in the release history ; those passes apply to the recorded commits and artifacts. Unit tests alone do not establish package/runtime success. Results, logs, and concurrent runs Use local cleanup to preview expired run logs/reports and explicitly selected retired output or Docker images. python3 nrpe.py clean does not delete anything; deletion requires --apply and respects workflow locks. Each build/test/verify invocation receives a unique run ID and writes: .nrpe/runs/<run-id>/ ├── report.json └── run.log # Created when a target reaches its workflow phases The JSON report includes UTC timestamps, action, per-target build/package/test outcomes, exit code, an optional normalized company CA SHA-256, and the tested artifact's filename, version from its filename, and SHA-256 hash. A summary distinguishes passed, failed, interrupted, running, and unrun phases. The first failure stops remaining targets; failed builds never test old output files. logs also shows errors that occur before container output exists. Local state and logs are ignored by Git and may contain paths or build output; review them before sharing. status matches test reports to the current package identity and hash. Replacing a package with different bytes invalidates its previous passed test status. A matching hash describes tested package bytes, not source provenance. The controller locks the target during each operation, preventing simultaneous controller builds or tests of that target. Different targets may run concurrently. Direct Compose commands do not participate in these locks; avoid mixing them with controller runs that use the same outputs. Ctrl+C stops the run's Compose process and removes only its uniquely named container. It does not run compose down or stop unrelated containers. If cleanup fails, the target lock is retained. After a terminal crash or forced process kill, status may show a lock and a report may remain running . Inspect .nrpe/locks/<target>/owner.json , the report, and docker ps -a before manually removing a stale lock directory. Never remove a lock while its run or container is still active. Existing Compose networks and builder caches are retained. Target server configuration The custom packages compile argument support while leaving runtime arguments disabled. On a real target server, deliberately configure /etc/nagios/nrpe.cfg on Debian, or /etc/nrpe.cfg for this SLES/OBS recipe: allowed_hosts = <nagios-server-ip>,127.0.0.1,::1 dont_blame_nrpe = 1 Replace the placeholder with the permitted Nagios server's address, review firewall rules, TLS, command definitions, and argument validation, then restart nagios-nrpe-server on Debian or nrpe on SLES. Bash command substitution must remain disabled. Build and test containers never apply these settings to the development host. Development and validation python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v for script in scripts/*.sh ; do bash -n " $script " || exit ; done python3 nrpe.py doctor For affected targets, run python3 nrpe.py verify <target> . Unit tests cover CLI routing, Docker diagnostics, run reports, artifact identity, locking, cleanup, and the Debian/RPM recipe transformations without requiring Docker or network access. They do not replace real package and integration tests. Windows-specific error messages and process handling also need validation on Windows. Implementation is in nrpe_cli/ ; nrpe.py is the public entry point. Docker runs build and test scripts from scripts/ . Root AGENTS.md and the additional script and test instructions apply. Write code, comments, documentation, and commits in English; follow Conventional Commits 1.0.0 . Repeatability and updates Current Debian sources and mutable image tags give a repeatable method, not bit-for-bit reproducible packages. Audit-ready releases require recording or pinning image digests, repository snapshots, source versions, and dependencies. Retain checksums and build information with released packages. Monitor Debian security updates and rebuild custom packages when official sources change; do not assume APT automatically replaces every custom version as intended. Official sources: Debian NRPE sources and source package information .

title: Contribute a field note
text: Useful field notes describe a real sequence of observations, including mistakes and unresolved questions. They are not endorsements or promises that a procedure works on every host. What to include Date, actual distribution/service pack, architecture and relevant tool versions. The initial symptom and the smallest test that helped narrow it down. Reviewed commands, expected/observed output and the actual outcome. Which changes were temporary, how they were cleaned up, and what remains untested. Attribution only to people who consent to being named. An anonymous project note is fine. Remove real hostnames, private addresses, credentials, keys, company certificates and confidential configuration. Use documentation addresses such as 192.0.2.10 . Never invent commands, successful outcomes or personal testimonials. How a note reaches the website Add a reviewed English Markdown file under website/content/ , with a title, date/platform line and introductory paragraph. The field-notes index and search include it automatically. Follow the project's contribution workflow : topic branch, review and integration into develop. Publication to gh-pages is a separate explicit maintainer action. There is no public submission form or unmoderated comment storage on this static website.

title: Service checks before TLS changes
text: Field note · 28 October 2026 · SLES 12 SP3 · NRPE 2.15 / check_nrpe 4.1.0 This account is based on the operator's reported commands and output during troubleshooting. Hostnames and addresses are anonymized. It is an observation from one deployment, not a recommendation to disable production TLS. The symptom The daemon logged Error: Could not complete SSL handshake. 1 . The initial discussion assumed SLES 15. Checking /etc/os-release , the installed RPM and linked libraries changed the picture: the host actually ran SLES 12 SP3 , NRPE 2.15-4.24 and OpenSSL 1.0.2j-fips with the OpenSSL 1.0 ABI. That mattered. A package built for SLES 15 could not be treated as a compatible replacement. Modern configuration directives also did not add certificate authentication support to the existing NRPE 2.15 executable. A smaller test, on a separate port The operator started a second daemon with a minimal configuration on port 15666, leaving the managed service on 5666 unchanged. Both client and test daemon used -n ; the client also used -2 for the old NRPE packet format. There were useful mistakes along the way: commands were initially run on a different host, a configured bind address was not local to that machine, and the test config's group permissions prevented the service user from reading it. On the intended server, NRPE 2.15 also rejected -f ; this version needed -d . Once those details were corrected, the reported response was: NRPE_PLAIN_OK The full isolated procedure records the configuration, checks and cleanup without requiring a systemd reload. What the result established The separate test confirmed basic NRPE communication and execution of a fixed command without TLS. A later temporary plaintext test on port 5666 also returned NRPE v2.15 and a successful check_load response with supplied thresholds. This narrowed the original problem toward TLS negotiation. It did not identify the exact cipher/certificate cause or prove a lasting TLS fix. Starting a manual daemon also did not make it a systemd-managed service: a second managed start failed because another NRPE process was already running. The operator's later clarification: start the missing service The operator later reported that the missing nrpe.service was the cause of their non-working checks: starting it alongside nagios.service restored the combined setup. A custom package was not needed to correct that service state. See the combined service and TLS FAQ for the service commands and the order of checks. This updates the outcome of the account. It does not establish that every previous handshake log entry came from a stopped daemon, or identify a cipher or certificate fix. The earlier manual/plaintext tests and the eventual managed service state are distinct observations. Confirm the current listener and repeat the actual monitoring check before changing TLS policy. What the custom build adds when it is actually needed The project now targets genuine SLES 12 SP3. Its NRPE 4.1.1 container checks cover certificate-authenticated TLS 1.2 against the original OpenSSL ABI; a separate modern OpenSSL client test also passed with server identity verification and a required client certificate. Those are separate test environments, not proof of installation on this operator's server. See the SLES TLS policy and validation limits before deployment. Temporary plaintext instances should be stopped and the intended managed service restored; no successful production upgrade or rollback is claimed in this note. The lesson to carry forward Check the managed service and listener first, then verify the host and OS before choosing a build target. Record the daemon and client versions, then test the smallest useful hypothesis. A successful plain connection is evidence about connectivity — not evidence that TLS is configured.
